scope: Spirit healer corpse-graveyard selection, cross-zone near transfer and persistence around ACK/logout

finding.before: Player::SaveToDB used pending destination coordinates for near and far transfers, but resolved the saved character-select zone only for far transfers. Logging out during a near teleport could therefore persist destination coordinates together with the source zone.
finding.reproduction: Native spirit healer activation with corpse graveyard5779 in Stormheim and ghost/healer graveyard4949 in Azsuna selected the correct near destination. Actual WorldSession logout deleted the Player and saved map1220/destination coordinates/health321/instance0, but zone7334 (Azsuna) instead of native7541 (Stormheim). Pinned pre-fix game.lib and .codex/spirit-graveyard-reference.log retain this failure.
finding.fix: Resolve savedZone whenever IsBeingTeleported() is true, matching the existing coordinate branch for near or far transfer. Keep the live far-save deferral, logout destination choice, source map cleanup, character flags and instance handling unchanged.

checks: Canonical Release worldserver/bnetserver build completed in build-extractors/bin/Release through original generated final-link libraries. No global OutDir override or runtime config change.

Test-TrialHelyaControlNative.ps1 -VerifyReleaseBinary passes24 new cases = three modes x four raid difficulties x Human/Orc. The fixture uses actual WorldSafeLocs5779/4949, native game_graveyard_zone links and native geometry; GetClosestGraveYard selects5779/4949, zones7541/7334. Healer6491 is spawned through native Creature initialization and its interaction admission is checked.

Native death/repop creates and saves the corpse at5779. Component movement places the ghost beside healer6491 at4949. Actual serialized SpiritHealerActivate decoding/handler invokes native resurrection, sickness and corpse conversion, then schedules a near teleport to the corpse graveyard; no manual resurrection or modeled destination-selection code.

Mode0 disconnects before near ACK using real WorldSession::Update -> LogoutPlayer and Player deletion. Mode1 sends the real near ACK, dispatches the native ZoneTeleport500ms session callback to complete outdoor zone-worker transfer, then performs real logout. Mode2 performs a normal live SaveToDB while near teleport is pending, then completes the near ACK and native zone callback for cleanup.

All24 SQL snapshots retain exact destination map/XYZ/orientation, zone7541, health321 and no ghost flag or resurrectable corpse. Actual logout rows are offline. Pending modes0/2 store instance0; completed mode1 stores current outdoor ZoneMap instance7541. Native zone worker IDs are not treated as foreign raid IDs.

Every case repeats the spirit request while transfer is pending after setting health321 and sickness duration598000. Pending destination, health and sickness duration remain unchanged. Successful ACK paths also repeat a near ACK; actual native callback arrival remains alive at the selected corpse graveyard with no remaining teleport flags.

Sixteen actual-logout cases construct a fresh socketless Player with the same GUID, restore saved health/flags, invoke native prepared aura/effect loaders and Player::LoadCorpse, then attach the real map factory selection at the verified saved destination. They remain alive/health321, retain sickness15007 and no ghost/corpse. A late spirit packet on the old Player-less session cannot change the fresh Player.

Existing88 graveyard/logout cases,40 complete ghost-return controls,32 prior ghost relog components, raid-instance mismatch/unloaded rejection/fallback and the configured Helya control checks also pass. New spirit cases do not change the earned raid encounter mask.

New Test-SpiritGraveyardRelease.ps1 retains the existing LogoutTeleport Release checks, compares current native source/library/executable hashes and verifies the exception-bounded canonical SaveToDB near-or-far gate encloses the native destination-zone resolver. Native ABI near26656/far26657 is used; incremental-link thunks are resolved. The live far-save deferral remains separately verified.

Test-CorpseRestartNative.ps1 -VerifyReleaseBinary also passes78 existing spirit healer interaction/penalty cases,48 corpse-reclaim cases, cold two-process corpse identity loading and startup/runtime expiry recovery. This checks the earlier living-player/duplicate-request fix against the newly built library.

Validation-owned hidden worldserver PID21308 reached ready and exited gracefully0. Startup DBErrors/stderr and native DBErrors are empty; Server logs contain no ERROR entries. No background servers remain. Scratch auth/character schemas and their SQL users are removed by the existing wrappers.

.codex/spirit-graveyard-native.log passed fixed mode0 and its fresh-Player reload, then rejected the fixture assumption that near ACK finishes all outdoor zone work. The ensuing native zone transfer retained a pending flag and instance0 in SQL; that was not another saved-zone defect.

.codex/spirit-graveyard-handoff.log used WorldPortAck to finish the zone handoff, but native ZoneTeleport keeps IsChangeMap and uses its own500ms session callback. Fixture now executes that actual FunctionProcessor callback with owned workers frozen; no production handoff change.

limits: Socketless Players, fixture-spawned healer6491, component ghost placement and decoded native handlers are used. No network authentication, client gossip dialog, client-driven movement or visual arrival is claimed.

Fresh-Player checks restore selected SQL health/flags and native aura/LoadCorpse components, then attach at the independently verified saved destination. They do not call aggregate Player::LoadFromDB, emulate offline time or prove full cold-server character recovery.

Transfers start and end on continent map1220 in different outdoor zones. The zone-worker transition after near ACK is exercised through its actual native callback. A Spirit Healer transfer between different continent maps, its connection/ACK failure handling, pet/camera state and durable inventory reload remain separate cases.

Actual client countdown/dialog, sickness display, corpse/bones appearance, movement release, zone loading and camera/pet portrait still require client verification. Successful compilation, startup and native code checks do not replace those.
